transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I keep getting these nagging thoughts that I forgot something important. It's... like I'll worry that I left my aunt’s medicine out wrong, or that I didn't set up my classroom materials safely for my students. And the frustrating part is, even when I know I probably handled it fine, that doubt just keeps popping back into my head.
When those doubts pop up, do you feel an urge to repeatedly check things, like going back to verify the medicine or classroom materials, to ease that feeling?

Yeah, I do. Um, before I leave the house or my classroom, I’ll usually go back over the same things a few times. Like, I'll check the pill organizer, or the stove... or at work, my lesson plans. Sometimes I just silently replay what I did in my head to make sure I handled it right. 

I basically keep checking or thinking about it until I finally feel calm enough to just move on. It’s... well, it makes me run late sometimes, which is pretty annoying.

Aside from these specific concerns about checking and safety, do you find yourself constantly worrying about a wide variety of other everyday topics, like your finances, personal health, or general future?

No, not really. Um, I mean, I think about my budget or regular life stuff sometimes, just like anyone else, but I wouldn't say I constantly worry about them. It's really just those specific things I mentioned... the checking, and making sure I didn't leave something unsafe or mess up at work. Outside of that, like with my health or the future, I feel pretty okay.
